newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium to cut public debt by 370 bln bfr end 1997.
newsitem.headline: Belgium to cut public debt by 370 bln bfr end 1997.

text.p: The Belgian government said on Tuesday it aimed to cut the country's public debt by 370 billion francs by the end of next year.
This will be achieved through a series of measures which include a 222 billion franc reduction of foreign currency debt by using central bank capital gains on past gold sales.
A second part will consist of the continued selling of public assets in enterprises up to an amount of 70 billion francs.

Another 75 billion francs will come from a more effective management of financial assets which public authorities hold, by investing these assets in public bonds rather than with financial institutions.

All these measures will come rapidly into effect due to the extended powers that parliament granted to the government in July, empowering it to take all necessary actions without prior parliamentary consent, a government statement said.
The 370 billion francs package should reduce Belgium's public debt as a percentage of gross domestic product to 127.0 percent in 1997 from 130.4 in 1996 and 137.0 percent in 1993.
"Thus the debt ratio will have fallen by 10 percent in a four-year period," Prime Minister Jean-Luc Deheane told parliament.
